candidates.lead: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
candidates.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

candidates.lead: The spectacle is just one of the many colourful tributes for Remembrance Day across north-west England
candidates.evidence_text: Memorial lit up for first time in a century as part of North West Remembrance tributes - BBC News Image source, Dave Mort Photography Image caption, The monument has been restored over a period of more than a decade By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 39 minutes ago A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day. The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Grange Hill and Wirral Borough Council. The spectacle is just one of a range of colourful tributes and events ahead of Remembrance Sunday across north-west England. They include a striking display of thousands of poppies and crosses on a roundabout in Leigh, Greater Manchester, while Poulton-le-Fylde in Lancashire, has a displayed more than a 1,000 yellow poppies to honour "forgotten heroines" who served their country. The Hoylake and West Kirby restoration project began in 2012 after a visitor tried to bring his father, a military veteran, to the memorial but found access virtually impossible. Years of neglect had left the site overgrown while the site's remembrance garden had almost disappeared. Image caption, Events and displays are happening across the region to mark Remembrance Sunday It inspired residents to set up the Friends of Grange Hill group which led the restoration of the memorial and ensure it was accessible to all. The landmark, which is perched on the highest point in West Kirby, will once again play a central role in community commemorations as it hosts West Kirby's Remembrance parade. But, for the first time, wreaths laid in honour of the fallen will be illuminated in the evening by new bespoke lighting. Image source, Dave Mort Photography Image caption, The landmark is perched on the highest point in West Kirby Derek Longman, chairman of the group, said it was a "proud moment". "What began as a small group of volunteers determined to rescue a neglected landmark has grown into a remarkable community effort," he said. "The new lighting scheme is not simply about illuminating a monument; it is about ensuring that the sacrifices commemorated here remain visible and remembered by future generations." Image source, Reeva Programme CIC handout Image caption, A roundabout in Leigh has been transformed into a war memorial display which includes thousands of poppies and white crosses Meanwhile, in Leigh, a busy roundabout near the Sports Village has been transformed into a Remembrance war memorial. Led by the Reeva Programme community interest company, the roundabout has been decorated with about 1,800 poppies and 1,000 white crosses, with four soldier figures in the centre of the display. The Woodland Makers group, which provides social events for veterans and emergency service leavers, produced the memorial with help from other community groups including schools and local Army and RAF cadets. Image source, Friends of Poulton Station Image caption, Poulton-le-Fylde railway station has been decorated with hundreds of yellow poppies in a nod to the Canary Girls Elsewhere, the Women of Wyre's Women's Institute organised a tribute to the Canary Girls, described as the "forgotten heroines" of both world wars, with Poulton-le-Fylde railway station and nearby St Chads Church decorated with more than a thousand yellow poppies. Peta Edwards who is the Lancashire ambassador for the Canary Girls Support Group, said the display would hopefully raise awareness of the million women who "made bullets and mixed chemicals with their bare hands" at home during the conflicts. Image source, Helen Nelson Image caption, St Mary's Church in Lymm, Cheshire, will be lined with 300 hand painted rocks for Sunday's Remembrance parade The munitions workers earned their nickname as their skin was often stained yellow by toxic chemicals as they risked their lives and limbs to supply ammunition to the frontline. "The Canary Girls were an amazing group who aren't recognised anywhere," Edwards said. "They were a beacon for us all and represent the spirit of the UK." She praised the local community - including Poulton's Knit and Natter group - for "pulling out all the stops" to make the 1,300 yellow poppies in time. candidates.evidence_text: Thousands of people are preparing to enjoy food, music and fireworks as Hindus across north-west England are set to celebrate Diwali About 600 are expected for the festival at the Gujarat Hindu Society in Preston, Lancashire, on Sunday, which opens with prayers and features a fireworks display finale Ishwer Tailor, vice president of the temple, which celebrated its 50th anniversary last year, said it had been planning the events for a month He said Diwali was a "fun" celebration where people come together at the temple throughout the day with the "spectacle" of the shrine decorated with lamps "and plenty of sweets for everyone" Diwali, or the Festival of Lights, is a five-day Hindu festival celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains It takes its name because houses, shops and public places are decorated with small oil lamps called diyas

candidates.evidence_text: After spending more than 20 years living in caravans and motorhomes, army veteran James Makinson said having a permanent home gave him one thing: "security" Known as Jimmy, the 79-year-old was helped into accommodation in Wigan through Homes at Ease, a housing programme run by the not-for-profit organisation Armed Forces Community HQ The scheme helps veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing their homes find permanent accommodation through social housing providers and private landlords. Since 2023, it has received more than 500 referrals across the North West "I can't say enough about this place," Makinson said of Armed Forces Community HQ, which helped him Lisa Murgatroyd, strategic development director at the organisation, said 99.5% of veterans housed through the scheme remained in permanent accommodation for more than six months Murgatroyd said much of the homelessness experienced by veterans was hidden, with people staying on friends' sofas or in insecure accommodation rather than sleeping rough

candidates.summary: The new road aims to reduce congestion on the single existing road in and out of Carrington in Trafford

candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: The new road aims to reduce congestion on the single existing road in and out of Carrington in Trafford
candidates.evidence_text: Carrington relief road approved despite hundreds of objections - BBC News Image caption, The council says Carrington Relief Road will take traffic away from the centre of the village By Richard Stead North West Published 6 November 2026 A controversial relief road plan has been approved despite hundreds of objections. The new road around Carrington in Trafford, first proposed more than a decade ago, will provide a new route to the M60 and reduce congestion in the village, the council said, as well as opening up the area for new housing. About 5,000 new homes could be built on land close to Manchester United's training ground. But objectors said the approval of the scheme was "heartbreaking", and it would have a devastating impact on wildlife. Liz Patel, deputy leader of Trafford Council, said: "This road has been decades in the making and it will offer residents in Partington an alternative route towards the M60. "The existing road is at maximum capacity and, by our modelling, the relief road will reduce congestion in the village of Carrington by 67%, as well as opening up the area for new homes while mitigating the biodiversity along the route." Image caption, Liz Patel, the Deputy Leader of Trafford Council, says the new road will help create new jobs The Carrington Relief Road is set to be a 2.7-mile single carriageway that would link the A6144 Manchester Road to an upgraded junction at Banky Lane/Carrington Spur. Half of the road would cross what is currently open farmland, while the other half would be built on the former Shell petrochemicals site, which closed in the 2000s. The route would include cycle lanes and specialist Pegasus crossings for horses. Image caption, Lorraine Eagling from the Friends of Carrington Moss says the new road will have a devastating impact on wildlife in the area When Trafford Council tabled plans to deliver the Carrington Relief Road, it caused uproar, with 680 letters of objection and a petition signed by more than 1,000 people. A further 191 objections were made during a second round of consultation. Lorraine Eagling, from the Friends of Carrington Moss, said: "It's heartbreaking because I've lived in this area all my life and everything here will be lost. "I see the wildlife, I see the skylarks, the lapwings, the buzzards and I've even seen deer on these fields, so its a unique environment." Image source, Trafford Council Image caption, The 2.7 mile Carrington Relief Road would have a single carriageway, Pegasus crossings for horse and cycle lanes. Objectors also claimed the plan would increase the number of cars passing through the area, with traffic from the M60 and M62 possibly using the route. Charlotte Waterworth, the Reform UK councillor for Bucklow St. Martins, said: "The objections are overwhelming and there are plenty of alternative brownfield sites to build houses on across Trafford, so the council should be listening to the residents. "You don't just live in this area for its charm, the neighbours and the community spirit, you live here for the beautiful scenery as well." Image caption, Reform UK councillor Charlotte Waterworth says the villages of Partington and Carrington cannot support thousands of new homes The main construction work on the Carrington Relief Road is set to start in 2029 should take about three years to complete. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Carrington relief road approved despite hundreds of objections - BBC News Image caption, The council says Carrington Relief Road will take traffic away from the centre of the village By Richard Stead North West Published 6 November 2026 A controversial relief road plan has been approved despite hundreds of objections. The new road around Carrington in Trafford, first proposed more than a decade ago, will provide a new route to the M60 and reduce congestion in the village, the council said, as well as opening up the area for new housing. About 5,000 new homes could be built on land close to Manchester United's training ground. But objectors said the approval of the scheme was "heartbreaking", and it would have a devastating impact on wildlife. Liz Patel, deputy leader of Trafford Council, said: "This road has been decades in the making and it will offer residents in Partington an alternative route towards the M60. "The existing road is at maximum capacity and, by our modelling, the relief road will reduce congestion in the village of Carrington by 67%, as well as opening up the area for new homes while mitigating the biodiversity along the route." Image caption, Liz Patel, the Deputy Leader of Trafford Council, says the new road will help create new jobs The Carrington Relief Road is set to be a 2.7-mile single carriageway that would link the A6144 Manchester Road to an upgraded junction at Banky Lane/Carrington Spur. Half of the road would cross what is currently open farmland, while the other half would be built on the former Shell petrochemicals site, which closed in the 2000s. candidates.lead: Sutton Community Fridge aims to reduce food waste and to help people who are struggling financially
candidates.evidence_text: A small food shed set up on a driveway in Cheshire less than two years ago has grown into a community hub which helps about 200 people each week Sutton Community Fridge was set up in December 2024 by Gayle Parks to tackle food waste and help families in the Macclesfield area access affordable food The project collects surplus stock from supermarkets, charities and businesses that would otherwise be thrown away and makes it available to buy at a low price The idea came to Gayle after about £15,000 worth of stock was stolen during a burglary at her family's pet shop In the aftermath, she relied on apps offering surplus food to help feed her own family She said: ''It made me question how could perfectly good food be going to waste when families were struggling to put food on their tables?''

candidates.evidence_text: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Grange Hill and Wirral Borough Council The spectacle is just one of a range of colourful tributes and events ahead of Remembrance Sunday across north-west England They include a striking display of thousands of poppies and crosses on a roundabout in Leigh, Greater Manchester, while Poulton-le-Fylde in Lancashire, has a displayed more than a 1,000 yellow poppies to honour "forgotten heroines" who served their country The Hoylake and West Kirby restoration project began in 2012 after a visitor tried to bring his father, a military veteran, to the memorial but found access virtually impossible Years of neglect had left the site overgrown while the site's remembrance garden had almost disappeared

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A neglected war memorial has been painstakingly restored by volunteers and lit up for the first time in its 104-year history ahead of Remembrance Day The Grade II* listed Hoylake and West Kirby monument has been transformed thanks to 14 years of renovations by the Friends of Grange Hill and Wirral Borough Council The spectacle is just one of a range of colourful tributes and events ahead of Remembrance Sunday across north-west England They include a striking display of thousands of poppies and crosses on a roundabout in Leigh, Greater Manchester, while Poulton-le-Fylde in Lancashire, has a displayed more than a 1,000 yellow poppies to honour "forgotten heroines" who served their country The Hoylake and West Kirby restoration project began in 2012 after a visitor tried to bring his father, a military veteran, to the memorial but found access virtually impossible Years of neglect had left the site overgrown while the site's remembrance garden had almost disappeared

Since 2023, it has received more than 500 referrals across the North West "I can't say enough about this place," Makinson said of Armed Forces Community HQ, which helped him Lisa Murgatroyd, strategic development director at the organisation, said 99.5% of veterans housed through the scheme remained in permanent accommodation for more than six months Murgatroyd said much of the homelessness experienced by veterans was hidden, with people staying on friends' sofas or in insecure accommodation rather than sleeping rough

candidates.evidence_text: A controversial relief road plan has been approved despite hundreds of objections The new road around Carrington in Trafford, first proposed more than a decade ago, will provide a new route to the M60 and reduce congestion in the village, the council said, as well as opening up the area for new housing About 5,000 new homes could be built on land close to Manchester United's training ground But objectors said the approval of the scheme was "heartbreaking", and it would have a devastating impact on wildlife Liz Patel, deputy leader of Trafford Council, said: "This road has been decades in the making and it will offer residents in Partington an alternative route towards the M60 "The existing road is at maximum capacity and, by our modelling, the relief road will reduce congestion in the village of Carrington by 67%, as well as opening up the area for new homes while mitigating the biodiversity along the route."

candidates.evidence_text: A small food shed set up on a driveway in Cheshire less than two years ago has grown into a community hub which helps about 200 people each week Sutton Community Fridge was set up in December 2024 by Gayle Parks to tackle food waste and help families in the Macclesfield area access affordable food The project collects surplus stock from supermarkets, charities and businesses that would otherwise be thrown away and makes it available to buy at a low price The idea came to Gayle after about £15,000 worth of stock was stolen during a burglary at her family's pet shop In the aftermath, she relied on apps offering surplus food to help feed her own family She said: ''It made me question how could perfectly good food be going to waste when families were struggling to put food on their tables?''

candidates.evidence_text: Train passengers are being warned over disruption this weekend, with direct services between Sheffield and Manchester cancelled entirely Network Rail said trains would be affected on Saturday and Sunday while work to replace the bridge deck at Beauchief, in Sheffield, is carried out Under the scheme, a new 73-tonne bridge deck, which carries the railway over the River Sheaf, will be lifted into place Ahead of the weekend's disruption, Network Rail's lead portfolio manager, Tom Grainger, said the company was "very sorry for any inconvenience" He said the work was essential to ensure the "continued safe running of the railway", adding that nearly 200ft (60m) of rail would also be renewed as part of the project As a result of the work, TransPennine Express services between Sheffield and Manchester Oxford Road via Stockport will not run this weekend, while trains between Sheffield and Manchester Piccadilly will be diverted to run via Huddersfield

candidates.evidence_text: Reform UK has insisted it supports plans for a new railway station in Bradford as part of Northern Powerhouse Rail (NPR), despite its opposition to parts of the broader project The party's deputy leader nationally, Richard Tice, said it had "never opposed" Phase 1 of NPR, which includes proposals for the city's new station, but remained against spending money on a high-speed line between Liverpool and Manchester However, questions remain over which parts of NPR Reform UK would support if it got into government, including a proposed new line connecting Bradford with Huddersfield and Manchester The city's Reform group say they do not believe the national stance poses a risk locally Bradford's political parties have all agreed on the importance of securing a new station as part of NPR, and specifically a through line, but opposition councillors have questioned whether the local Reform administration's commitment is shared by the party nationally At a meeting of Bradford Council's Reform-led executive earlier this week, Conservative group leader Rebecca Poulsen welcomed the proposed new station's city-centre location but said Bradford needed more than a replacement terminus

candidates.evidence_text: A building developer has been ordered to pay more than £45m to the government after fire safety defects were repaired in seven high-rise buildings The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash
candidates.what_happened: Developer Urban Splash forced to pay £45m over Manchester fire safety works

A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash Judge Jonathan Holbrook, sitting with two other First Tier Tribunal members, said in a 260-page judgment there was a "powerful case" for the developer "rather than the taxpayer, to bear the remediation costs"

Videos from the scene showed a shirtless man sitting on the top of Adelphi Weir in the river, clinging on to a nearby At one point he can be seen almost lying down in an apparent attempt to avoid falling over the edge, over which a strong current is flowing down a drop of several metres A nearby resident who rang 999 told the M.E.N he seemed 'trapped' on the edge of the waterfall Officers from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service attended the scene. The man can be seen shuffling along the edge of the weir on his bottom before rescuers come to his aid, carrying him in a fireman's lift back to dry land

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police How plans for a radical reform of UK policing may affect Greater Manchester Police 'Everybody needs to look a bit more like us' Sir Stephen Watson said today as chiefs made a call for a radical restructuring of the country's Greater Manchester Police (GMP) would not necessarily be merged with neighbouring forces as part of a radical reform of policing, which a number of senior officers have called for, the force’s chief constable has said The leader of GMP, Sir Stephen Watson, was among the speakers at an event in Manchester today (Friday, November 6) where the Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police, Sir Mark Rowley, warned UK policing ‘will fail’ if it doesn’t ‘urgently reform.’ In a keynote speech, Sir Mark said the country has 43 ‘overstretched’ police forces ‘trying to do too much with too little’ and needed to drastically reshape its current ‘fragmented, bureaucratic, top-heavy spaghetti model.’ He said he believed it should be restructured into one national police service and ‘eight to ten regional police forces' alongside hundreds of 'local police commands.' The proposal has faced resistance from some police and crime commissioners and local leaders who fear a restructuring will cost money and weaken ties between senior officers and the communities they serve

View 3 Images Thousands of Airbnbs across Greater Add to preferred sources News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 07:57, 07 Nov 2026 Airbnb hosts in and around Greater Manchester have welcomed the changes to chore requirements Airbnb has announced, which come into force later this month. But they’ve warned that there are more concerning From November 20, changes to Airbnb's ‘house rules’ policy will come into effect. From that date hosts will have to choose from seven standard rules, with anything else being stipulated as a request Under the updated policy, hosts can make ‘reasonable requests’ regarding cleaning and rubbish, however Airbnb has clarified on its website what hosts cannot ask. Under the new rules hosts can no longer ask guests to: wash dishes and put them away, strip the bed, remove rubbish of They can ask guests to put used dishes in the sink, gather together used towels and turn off amenities before leaving. The changes have divided opinion online, with some guests thrilled at no longer being asked to complete numerous tasks at checkout while some hosts fear it could View 3 Images Holly Stott operates two Airbnbs in Ramsbottom, including Alfred's (Image: Holly Stott)

candidates.evidence_text: Tameside Dispersal order issued in Greater Manchester after fireworks 'aimed at public and officers' Eight arrests were made in Tameside on Bonfire Night Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:03, 06 Nov 2026 Updated 1 Greater Manchester Police have issued a 72-hour dispersal order for a Tameside district after reports of disorder and fireworks being 'aimed at officers' The order covers the St Peter's area of Ashton-under-Lyne town centre, bordered by Lord Sheldon Way, Oldham Road, Richmond Street and the A635, and is in place until Saturday evening (November 7), having come into effect at 9pm yesterday (November 5) The section 34 order gives officers powers to direct 'anyone causing or likely to cause' anti-social behaviour, crime or disorder to leave the area, or face the possibility of arrest and prosecution The force said the order, the third such order to be issued in the past day, follows 'ongoing disorder' and incidents of anti-social behaviour and fireworks being 'aimed and targeted at members of the public and [GMP] officers' Local councillor Kaleel Khan was posting updates on his Facebook page throughout the night, posting videos which showed wheelie bins on fire and fireworks being thrown near to Millennium Green Park. He called the scenes 'shocking'

Objectors also fear the plan could actually increase the number of cars passing through the area, with traffic from the nearby M60 and However, following a fractious council planning meeting on Thursday night (November 5), the scheme was narrowly approved by a vote of seven to six. Objectors in the public gallery could be heard shouting ‘it’s a disgrace’ following the decision

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts New murder suspect, 26, named after man stabbed to death in Moss Side A 26-year-old man is in custody Add to preferred sources News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 21:53, 06 Nov 2026 View Image Adrian Brown (Image: Facebook) A second man has been charged in relation to the fatal stabbing of a father-of-three in Moss Side six months ago Adrian Brown, 34, a father of three who was known to many as Dre, was found with stab wounds to the chest on Raby Street in Moss Side on the evening of May 8 this year He was rushed to hospital but sadly died of his injuries. Now, a 26-year-old man has been charged with his murder Greater Manchester Police said Emeil Lee, 26, currently of HMP Forest Bank, has been charged with murder. He appeared at the same court on Thursday (November 5) where he was remanded into local authority care

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police How plans for a radical reform of UK policing may affect Greater Manchester Police 'Everybody needs to look a bit more like us' Sir Stephen Watson said today as chiefs made a call for a radical restructuring of the country's Greater Manchester Police (GMP) would not necessarily be merged with neighbouring forces as part of a radical reform of policing, which a number of senior officers have called for, the force’s chief constable has said The leader of GMP, Sir Stephen Watson, was among the speakers at an event in Manchester today (Friday, November 6) where the Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police, Sir Mark Rowley, warned UK policing ‘will fail’ if it doesn’t ‘urgently reform.’ In a keynote speech, Sir Mark said the country has 43 ‘overstretched’ police forces ‘trying to do too much with too little’ and needed to drastically reshape its current ‘fragmented, bureaucratic, top-heavy spaghetti model.’ He said he believed it should be restructured into one national police service and ‘eight to ten regional police forces' alongside hundreds of 'local police commands.' The proposal has faced resistance from some police and crime commissioners and local leaders who fear a restructuring will cost money and weaken ties between senior officers and the communities they serve

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Pensioner said she was assaulted by a Boots security guard - but it was all an elaborate lie Annette Gallimore has now been hauled before the courts Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 14:07, 06 Nov 2026 View 2 Images A A pensioner made up an elaborate bogus story that she was assaulted and seriously injured by a security guard inside a Boots store in a bid to claim compensation The tables have been turned on Annette Gallimore, however, as she's now been convicted of fraud by false representation and ordered to pay out thousands of pounds herself Gallimore, 69, falsely claimed she was knocked over by a security guard in a Boots store in Bolton, causing torn ligaments in her knee and bruising, police said She claimed it happened when she went to collect a shopping basket - and said she went on to be treated for her alleged injuries in hospital. Police said Gallimore, of Dudley Avenue, Bolton, subsequently 'attempted to pursue a compensation claim' against Aviva, whose insurance po But smelling a rat, Aviva referred the case to The Insurance Fraud Enforcement Department (IFED) - a unit within the City of London Police dedicated to combatting insurance fraud

candidates.evidence_text: Middleton Environment Agency called to Middleton river after 'four foot high' foam spotted The incident has been reported to the Envrionment Agency Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 10:16, 06 Nov 2026 Updated 10:26, Environment Agency was called after a ‘four foot’ tall block of foam appeared along the River Irk in Middleton . The soapy substance, described as having a ‘chemically smell', was spotted by locals on Wednesday (October 4) Jamie Clayton , a fishery manager from the Manchester Anglers Club, was among the first to report the incident to Environment Agency when he came across the phenomena at Rhodes Lodges just of Manchester Old Road He told the M.E.N: “I’ve seen it loads. I’ve seen posts about it loads, but this is the first time I’ve seen it this bad. I’m going to say the froth is around four foot high. The river’s got a constant smell to it around here “It is a chemically smell and yesterday it was the same smell as most days, just stronger.” This isn’t the first time the foam has come up in the river this year. In August, another investigation was launched when a huge 'foam iceberg' was reported by locals

candidates.evidence_text: Carrington Carrington relief road has 1,000 against it and makes some 'ashamed to be human', but it will be happening The major relief road will unloock the wider redevelopment of Carrington and Partington and deliver thousands of new homes Add to pre The controversial Carrington relief road plan has been approved, despite hundreds of objections. For decades, the relief road has been seen as the solution to traffic woes in the Partington and Carrington areas of Trafford Diverting traffic away from the overly congested A6144 is seen as one of the major goals of the project. But when Trafford council tabled plans to finally deliver Carrington Relief Road, it caused uproar, with 680 letters of objection and a petition signed by over 1,000 people To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Campaigners claimed the scheme will eat up a chunk of Carrington Moss nature reserve, destroying wildlife habitats and ecosystems along with it. Objectors also fear the plan could actually increase the number of cars passing through the area, with traffic from the nearby M60 and However, following a fractious council planning meeting on Thursday night (November 5), the scheme was narrowly approved by a vote of seven to six. Objectors in the public gallery could be heard shouting ‘it’s a disgrace’ following the decision

candidates.evidence_text: Russell Brand BBC issue statement and apology after Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault Brand is a former Radio 2 presenter Add to preferred sources News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 06:33, 06 Nov 2026 View 3 Images Russell Brand and wi The BBC has said 'there can be no place for the abuse of power' as it reiterated its public apology following the conviction of former Radio 2 presenter Russell Brand Brand, 51, is facing a lengthy prison sentence after being found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others during his showbusiness career Following his convictions, a BBC spokesperson said: “Firstly, the thoughts of everyone at the BBC are with the brave women who came forward and told their stories which led to a conviction in this case. There can be no place for the abuse of power “Across the industry, we must work together to ensure that anyone who suffers at someone else’s hand feels able to report it, that their concerns are taken seriously and that they are listened to “We published a detailed report in January 2025 into how complaints about Russell Brand’s conduct were handled. This looked at eight allegations of misconduct while he worked here between 2006 and 2008

candidates.lead: The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night
candidates.evidence_text: The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night Share on WhatsApp Share via Email A visual showing the proposed Carrington Relief Road Trafford councillors have narrowly approved plans for the controversial Carrington Relief Road, despite hundreds of objections and warnings about the impact on Green Belt land and wildlife The decision was made by just seven votes to six at a fractious planning committee meeting last night, with members of the public gallery reportedly shouting "it's a disgrace" as the result was announced The road is considered essential to unlocking New Carrington, Trafford's largest housing and employment allocation, which could eventually deliver around 5,000 homes and 350,000 square metres of employment space Although the route lies around three miles north of Altrincham, the development could have wider implications for traffic, housing demand and public services across the borough The approximately 4km road would link the A6144 Manchester Road near Carrington and Partington with the Carrington Spur towards Sale

The brewery is specifically looking for a couple to take on the pub, offering a salary of £28,725 per person, a large manager's flat above the premises with all utilities paid, and free training

candidates.evidence_text: The buildings in Manchester, developed by Urban Splash between 2000 and 2008, were alleged to have serious defects discovered in inspections after the Grenfell Tower disaster The extent of the defects was disputed but they have been fixed at a cost of more than £60m, with about £51.1m paid from the government's Building Safety Fund (BSF) established after the disaster The buildings were not owned by Urban Splash at the time of the remediation work and no BSF money was paid to it. A spokesperson said the scale of the liability was "significant" The Department of Housing, Communities and Local Government brought a case to a specialist tribunal, seeking an order for the developer to contribute towards the cost of the works paid from the taxpayer-supported fund On Thursday, the tribunal ruled that more than £45.7m should be paid to the government by Urban Splash Judge Jonathan Holbrook, sitting with two other First Tier Tribunal members, said in a 260-page judgment there was a "powerful case" for the developer "rather than the taxpayer, to bear the remediation costs"

If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect thei This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November

candidates.title: Oldham to light up with spectacular free programme of events for Autumn/Winter 2026
candidates.summary: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Validator: news item is 24 days old (hard cutoff 14d), dropped regardless of update wording.

candidates.lead: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026
candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

Rochdale firm, Winterburns, is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools Working with local employers Seddon, the council oversaw repairs and improvements at more than half a dozen schools, benefitting over 3,000 pupils from primary to secondary age The wide-ranging work was carried out over the summer break to minimise disruption The project saw some schools receiving new boilers and water heaters, new roof installed at one primary school, while another had more energy efficient windows installed Some fire alarm systems and emergency lighting have also been upgraded It is the second school decarbonisation project Seddon has delivered with Bolton Council, helping to improve the efficiency and long-term sustainability of school buildings across the borough

candidates.evidence_text: Representatives from WWL NHS Trust and Wigan Grammar School Old Boys Association Wigan Grammar School has been formally recognised with a blue plaque at the site of its former building. Founded in 1597, Wigan Grammar School taught countless pupils in a history spanning almost four centuries and served as one of the town’s oldest continuously operating institu On Wednesday 28th October, a selection of former pupils, Wigan Council and Wrightington, Wigan, and Leigh NHS Trust representatives attended the unveiling of the blue plaque at the Thomas Linacre Centre, which housed the school from 1937 until its closure in 1972. Councillor Chri “This blue plaque is a fitting recognition of the school’s remarkable legacy, ensuring that its story is remembered and celebrated for years to come.” Gaining a reputation for excellence that persisted through the centuries, Wigan Grammar School’s pupils have been represented in fields as diverse as neurology, print making, engineering and nuclear energy Some famous alumni include acclaimed composer Sir Ernest Bullock as well as actor Sir Ian McKellen

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . Blending humour, honesty and heartfelt stor On stage, a constantly changing world of cardboard boxes transforms before your eyes, creating a playful and inventive setting for the performance. Throughout the show, artists CickinDunt create live portraits of audience members, turning the theatre into a one-night-only gallery Warm, thought-provoking and often funny, LOVE**WORK brings together stories from different places and perspectives to celebrate the experiences that connect us all. Expect an imaginative evening of theatre that sparks conversation, reflection and plenty of moments of recognition ★★★★ 'It is life itself laid bare. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Italian small plates, handmade pasta, and pizza That’s right Stopfordians – we’re gaining yet another brand new addition to our town’s blooming food and drink scene, as Social Osteria opens its doors at Weir Mill It’s safe to say we’re in good hands, with the geniuses behind The Social Trattoria, named best Trattoria at the Italian Awards UK 2025, being the ones to bring this new taste of Italy to South Manchester Just because we are no longer experiencing the weather to match an Italian summer, doesn’t mean we can’t continue eating like we’re there Social Osteria can now be found overlooking the River Mersey, as a beautiful 2,000 sq ft space within the buzzing new canalside development, fully equipped with the classic exposed red brickwork, vaulted ceilings and even the restored original kiln As you approach the restaurant, you are greeted by a sunken courtyard and riverside seating, making for the perfect alfresco dining spot, when the warmer weather finally rolls back around

evidence_packet.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
evidence_packet.summary: Stay connected. Know what's next
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

That depends who you ask... - Prolific North Skip to content News Wise Owl gets another order of Our Farm Next Door News Data organisation appoints Vikas Shah Agency Reboot strengthens senior team How much do students use AI for their studies? That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Researchers argue that universities need to move beyond treating AI primarily as a technical challenge or a threat to academic integrity, and develop a better understanding of how students and staff engage with it. The research examined how academic staff and students perceived their own use of generative AI tools, as well as their views of how the technology was being used in higher education. The study surveyed 45 academic staff and 86 students in a school covering social science disciplines at a UK research-intensive university. The questionnaires were conducted between April and June 2024, so essentially before AI took over the likes of Google whether you asked it to or not. When asked about students’ use of AI for academic purposes, staff gave an average rating of 5.23 on a seven-point scale. Students’ own responses produced an average of just 3.11. The researchers caution that students may have underreported their use of AI, but say the difference nevertheless points to the limited information staff may have about how students use these tools in their studies. AI use can be difficult for lecturers to identify, particularly when they see only the final version of an assignment rather than the process through which it was produced. Students may also use AI independently of their interactions with teaching staff, leaving academics with an incomplete picture of their working practices. The research also found that students were generally more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI. Students rated the technology more highly in terms of its likely contribution to academic performance, including helping them learn about their subjects, increasing productivity and reducing workloads. They also felt more strongly than staff that appropriate conditions and support were in place to help them use AI tools. Among the uses identified in the survey, students reported using generative AI to find answers to questions and assignments, generate written work, and translate or improve the grammar of their writing. The researchers suggest that the immediate appeal of AI tools may lie in their ability to produce and improve text. However, they also argue that universities need to understand the range of ways students use the technology, rather than assume that its role in academic work is straightforward. The study also found considerable variation in staff members’ familiarity with AI. While 63 per cent of academic staff respondents had used at least one generative AI tool in the six months before the survey, some had limited practical experience of the technology. candidates.evidence_text: £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans - Prolific North Skip to content News Wise Owl gets another order of Our Farm Next Door News Data organisation appoints Vikas Shah Agency Reboot strengthens senior team £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 A Manchester-based fintech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million to automate the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. The company uses AI to automate much of that work, which is typically spread across spreadsheets, PDFs, emails and other disconnected systems. Aggregating this data manually can sometimes take up to several days, but Crediflow says its platform reduces that time to between 10 and 30 minutes, giving credit teams more time to concentrate on critical tasks. READ MORE: Leeds financial tech consultancy merges with London cloud specialist In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts, a process the industry calls financial spreading, analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. The funding will accelerate development of the company’s platform, support engineering and product hires, and help Crediflow serve more banks and specialist lenders. Crediflow will also extend automation across the loan lifecycle, with workflows tailored to each lender’s credit policies and processes. By bringing origination, underwriting and monitoring together, Crediflow aims to reduce repeated work and help lenders grow their loan books without an associated increase in administrative costs. Last year, Crediflow became one of eight companies to receive funding from PXN’s PraeSeed programme, a 12-week cohort-based investment programme run in partnership with the British Business Bank and NPIF II to help scale early-stage businesses. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. Drey founded Crediflow after seeing first-hand how manual processes constrain lenders’ ability to grow. Drey Kenfack, CEO and founder of Crediflow AI, said: “Growing a loan book takes more than finding borrowers and having capital available. You need the capacity to assess those businesses, get decisions through approval and stay on top of risk once the money is out the door. I’ve spent much of my career doing that work. “When every transaction requires hours of manual preparation, it affects how much business a lender can take on and which deals are worth pursuing. We built Crediflow to bring that workload down and give credit teams more time to understand the borrower and structure the financing.” Joe Ball, senior investment associate at PXN Ventures , added: “Businesses of all sizes and across all sectors often rely on commercial finance for a multitude of reasons, but the processes involved in granting this finance are often largely manual, making the process inefficient and slowing down lending decisions. By automating this area of the sector, Drey and the Crediflow AI team are not just supporting lenders but also removing barriers for companies that need funding to grow.” Jonathan Keeling, partner at Haatch, said: “The best B2B founders build the product they wished they’d had in their last job. Drey spent over a decade in credit roles watching good deals stall on admin, and Crediflow turns hours of manual spreading and memo writing into structured analysis credit teams can act on.

candidates.evidence_text: US giant NetApp completes acquisition of Manchester’s Peak AIO Posted on November 6, 2026 by staff US giant NetApp completes acquisition of Manchester’s Peak AIO Nasdaq-listed data platform swoops for firm addressing industry's most demanding data-intensive computing challenges Share: Listen to article Deals Nasdaq-listed US giant NetApp has completed its acquisition of Manchester AI firm PEAK AIO. PEAK AIO was founded in Manchester by Mark Klarzynski and was designed to address some of the industry’s most demanding data-intensive computing challenges. The company’s core innovation, a next-generation metadata architecture and high-performance parallel file system, was developed to solve one of the defining infrastructure challenges of the AI era: enabling shared storage to scale alongside the GPU clusters that power modern AI workloads. The deal, for an undisclosed amount, has now secured regulatory approvals. Investor Pembroke VCT plc, a London-listed venture capital trust, said it would generate a significant return for shareholders. “NetApp and PEAK:AIO were built around the shared conviction that the AI era needs data infrastructure designed to scale to extraordinary levels,” said Mark Klarzynski, chief technology officer and founder at PEAK:AIO. “With the acquisition by NetApp, we can bring our innovation together with the reach, expertise, and trusted customer relationships of a global data infrastructure leader. Together, we are well positioned to help define what comes next and deliver technology that makes managing data for the AI era more practical, efficient, and accessible.” £178m ticketing giant Skiddle secures first external investment Syam Nair, chief product officer at NetApp, added: “The AI factory is only as productive as its data pipeline. By combining NetApp’s unified storage with PEAK:AIO’s metadata architecture, we separate metadata from data so performance scales out with concurrency, and we do it with open standards rather than proprietary clients. “Customers can run more AI workloads, on their existing infrastructure, with the security, resilience, and simplicity of enterprise data management.” George Kurian, CEO at NetApp, said: “AI infrastructure is reaching unprecedented scale, demanding a new approach to storage built from the ground up. “By combining PEAK:AIO’s expertise in metadata services and parallel namespace innovation with the proven scale, data management capabilities, and enterprise-grade services of the NetApp Platform, we are leapfrogging the market as we deliver our next-generation, zettabyte-scale architecture to support the growth of AI clouds and GPU-as-a-service providers.” New images reveal latest plans for £500m Therme Manchester Related Stories View All Could AI firm’s director be key to Poundland rescue bid? This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Eat, meet, drink, shop, watch, talk, listen, laugh. Come in, be yourself and if you like it bring your friends! Altrincham’s charter dates back to 1290, it’s location at the intersection of the Cheshire farm belt and the commercial commuter zone of Manchester means the town has a long and important history. Altrincham market is now at the heart of the regeneration of ‘the modern market tow The covered market hosts regional food producers, vintage fashion and furniture, home & garden and contemporary craft on a Tuesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday Altrincham Market House Opening Hours Tues-Sat : 9am-10pm Sun : 9am-6pm Mon : Closed The Outdoor Market (Shopping) Tues: 8am-3pm Fri: 8am-3pm Sat: 8am-4pm Sun: 10am-4pm Altrincham Market House is home to award-winning independent quality food operators. candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. View Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Tyrone Marshall Manchester United Correspondent 05:00, 07 Nov 2026 Michael Carrick bought himself some breathing space with the dramatic win against Roma on Tuesday, but he might need another positive result against Aston Villa on Sunday Carrick's future has been the subject of intense scrutiny in recent weeks, and he survived by the skin of his teeth after back-to-back defeats to Como and Bournemouth by three-goal margins Before the Roma fixture, there was a growing expectation within football circles that he would be dismissed next week, but victory has somewhat changed the narrative While Manchester United's decision-makers accept their share of responsibility for wider issues at the club and not giving Carrick all the tools he needed, doubts had grown earlier this week as to whether the 45-year-old was the right man to dig them out of this crisis Alternative options have been looked at, although the lack of a clear alternative is a drawback to pressing ahead with change. Director of football Jason Wilcox is a big admirer of Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler and the work Unai Emery has done at Villa Park is also admired within

candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
